purpose: Work around missing MUSA tree-verify topk>1 by a CPU tree walk, to measure NGRAM acceptance and speed.
config: 96 experts / 32K / FP16 KV / external corpus 1.55M tokens / draft 6 / external SAM budget 4

results.prompt: exact copy of a systemd unit
results.note: copy succeeds; no accept counter in this run

conclusion: CPU tree-walk makes NGRAM functionally runnable on MUSA, but end-to-end decode is far slower than the 20 tok/s baseline because every verify step performs CPU readback/sync. No NGRAM speedup. A native MUSA topk>1 tree-verify kernel is required; 160/64K also cannot keep >6GB with FP16 KV and NGRAM verify workspace.
